For your Quarto/GitHub Pages site, I’d use Calendly + Stripe for the quickest route to paid bookings. You can embed Calendly directly in a .qmd page, and it supports collecting payment when someone books, including in euros. The upfront-payment feature requires an eligible Calendly plan.
Calendly Help
+1
The setup can cover both online and in-person lessons, each lasting 60 minutes. You don’t need to build a payment system or store card details yourself.

title: Teaching to do list
text:
1. Set up the booking service

Create a Calendly account at calendly.com.
Connect your calendar (Google Calendar or Outlook) so that booked slots aren’t double-booked.
Connect Stripe in Calendly under Integrations & apps → Stripe. You’ll need a Stripe account to receive payments.

Calendly Help
Create two 60-minute event types: - Online English Lesson — 60 minutes - In-person English Lesson — 60 minutes
Give each event its own availability and meeting/location instructions.
In each event’s payment settings, enable Require payment to book, select Stripe, set your price in euros, and add your cancellation/refund terms.

Calendly Help

You can decide whether the in-person lesson happens at your home, at a mutually agreed location, or somewhere else; the event description should make that clear before a student pays.

title: What is connected speech?
text:
When people speak naturally, words do not always sound as they appear in a dictionary. Sounds may link across word boundaries, become weaker, or change in predictable ways.
This is part of connected speech. Understanding it can help learners both recognise spoken English and make their own speech flow more naturally.

title: What is connected speech?
text:
What can happen?

Linking: the end of one word connects smoothly to the beginning of the next.
Weak forms: common grammatical words may have a reduced vowel when they are unstressed.
Assimilation: a sound may become more like a neighbouring sound.
Elision: a sound may be omitted in some contexts.

The details vary by accent, speaking style and context. The goal is not to force every feature into your speech, but to develop awareness and practise the patterns that help you communicate.

I’m Dr Des Ryan, an English language teacher and linguist with extensive experience teaching international learners and university students. I hold a PhD in Linguistics from Trinity College Dublin and have taught English since 2007, working with learners from beginner to advanced level.
My approach combines practical teaching with a detailed understanding of how English works. I explain the patterns behind pronunciation, grammar and spelling, then help you apply them through structured practice and feedback.
Get in touch by email · LinkedIn · Academic profile and papers

What I can help you with



Spoken English and pronunciation
Work on clarity, intelligibility, rhythm and connected speech. Understand not just what to practise, but why particular sounds and patterns can be difficult.



Academic English
Develop presentations, seminar contributions, essays and research communication. Practise organising ideas and expressing complex points clearly.



Professional communication
Prepare for meetings, interviews, workplace conversations and presentations. Build language that is clear, appropriate and natural for your context.

title: About Des
text:
Teaching experience

English language teacher
2007–present
I have taught English to learners at a range of levels, designing lessons in speaking, listening, pronunciation, grammar and writing. I adapt materials and explanations to each learner’s goals, existing knowledge and areas for development.


University lecturer and academic skills tutor
UCD, Trinity College Dublin, TU Dublin and University of Galway · 2012–2017
I taught academic writing, research skills and communication to undergraduate and postgraduate students. This included helping students structure essays, prepare presentations, communicate research and approach academic study with greater confidence.


Machine learning / voicebuilding engineer
Apple · 2020–2024
I worked on improving the naturalness of English speech for Siri. This technical role drew on linguistic analysis and strengthened my interest in pronunciation, spoken language and what makes speech sound clear and natural. It gives me a useful perspective on the relationship between the way English is described and the way it is actually spoken.


Tour guide
Rome and Dublin · 2009–2011
Guiding international groups developed my skills in storytelling, public speaking and explaining unfamiliar ideas to people from different backgrounds.

title: About Des
text:
Academic background

PhD in Linguistics, Trinity College Dublin — research on how English spelling is formed and how spelling relates to sound and word structure.
MSc in Linguistics (Distinction), University of Edinburgh.
Higher Diploma in Data Analytics (Distinction), National College of Ireland.
BA in Mathematics (First Class Honours), Trinity College Dublin.
BA in English Literature, Trinity College Dublin.

My doctoral research was supported by the Irish Research Council. It investigated the principles that shape English spelling, including the ways spelling represents pronunciation, distinguishes words and preserves relationships between related forms.

title: About Des
text:
Selected publications and research
My academic work focuses on English spelling and writing systems. That research also informs the way I teach: English is easier to understand when learners can see the patterns behind what might otherwise seem arbitrary.

Ryan, Des. Principles of English Spelling Formation. PhD thesis, Trinity College Dublin, 2018. Read the thesis in Trinity’s research repository.
Cook, Vivian and Des Ryan (eds.). The Routledge Handbook of the English Writing System. Routledge, 2016.
Ryan, Des. “Google Doodles: Evidence of How Graphemes’ Colour, Shape, Size and Position Can Interact to Make Writing Multidimensional.” Writing Systems Research, 2015.
Ryan, Des. “Grammaphonology: A New Theory of English Spelling.” SKASE Journal of Theoretical Linguistics, 2011.
Ryan, Des. “Linguists’ Descriptions of the English Writing System.” In The Routledge Handbook of the English Writing System, edited by Vivian Cook and Des Ryan, 2016.

Browse my academic profile and available papers.

title: About Des
text:
How I teach
I aim to make lessons clear, focused and collaborative. I explain the reasoning behind a language point, give you opportunities to practise it, and use feedback to identify what will help you progress next.
You do not need to know linguistic terminology to benefit from this approach. I use technical detail when it makes something clearer, and keep the focus on your goals: communicating more comfortably, accurately and effectively.
My background in linguistics, university teaching and speech technology means I can work both with the bigger picture and with specific questions about sounds, words, grammar or writing.

title: About Des
text:
A little more about me
I’m based in Wicklow, Ireland. Alongside teaching and linguistics, I’m interested in cycling, travel writing and storytelling. I speak English, French and some Irish, and I value the intercultural awareness that comes from working with learners with different languages and experiences.
